questions.prompt: Voltaire’s line Hicks quotes, about enlightened people arguing a long time, is used to warn that:
choices: A Logic is useless once people are witty.
B The question may not be clear—concepts and word-use have gone fuzzy.
C All long arguments are therefore valid.
D We should replace concepts with sensations only.
questions.explain: Long disputes among sharp thinkers often mean the question isn’t clear; concepts need attention.

questions.prompt: In the cognitive hierarchy Hicks sketches, what are percepts?
choices: A Pure numbers with no sensory origin.
B Integrations of sensations into awareness of objects.
C Finished scientific theories.
D Synonyms for informal fallacies.
questions.explain: Bundles of sensations are integrated into percepts; we then are aware of objects in the environment.

questions.prompt: When a child uses “dog” for the family dog and also for a dog on the street, Hicks treats that as evidence the child is:
choices: A Using a proper name for one percept only.
B Designating a class—operating at the conceptual level.
C Still stuck at isolated color patches with no integration.
D Committing an ad hominem.
questions.explain: “Dog” is not a proper name for one animal; it names a class of things.

questions.prompt: The speckled-hen example is meant to show that counting the speckles:
choices: A Improves raw visual perception of the hen automatically.
B Is a learned conceptual achievement that perception alone does not give.
C Proves hens have no identity.
D Is an informal fallacy of majority.
questions.explain: You don’t perceive the number of speckles; counting uses mathematical concepts and does not make the hen look clearer.

questions.prompt: Why does Hicks say adult arguments about God or political labels should start with conceptual work?
choices: A Because definitions are optional decoration after the fight.
B Because we must get clear what we are talking about before plunging into for/against arguments.
C Because concepts are impossible for adults.
D Because Voltaire forbade political words.
questions.explain: Before arguing whether God exists or whether someone is a socialist, get the concept clear or the discussion talks past itself.
